question: Who is the only living representative of the extremely ancient and diverse group, Sphenopsida, commonly known as ‘horsetails’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Equisetum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Equisetum (Horsetails):**

 
 
• Ancient Lineage: Equisetum represents one of the oldest surviving genera of plants, with fossil records dating back over 300 million years to the Carboniferous period. They are considered "living fossils".
 
• Sphenopsida Class: They belong to the class Sphenopsida, a group of plants that were much more diverse and prominent in the past.
 
• Hollow Stems: Equisetum species have distinctive hollow, jointed stems that are often ribbed.
 
• Silica Content: Their cell walls are heavily impregnated with silica, giving them a rough texture and making them useful for scouring.
 
• Reproduction: They reproduce by spores, not seeds, and have underground rhizomes for vegetative spread.
 
• Ecological Role: Often found in damp or marshy environments.
 
• Common Name: Known as horsetails or scouring rushes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Psilotum (Whisk Ferns):**

 
 
• Ancient and Simple: Psilotum is another ancient lineage of vascular plants, often referred to as "living fossils." They are considered among the simplest of extant vascular plants.
 
• Lack of True Roots and Leaves: They lack true roots and leaves, instead having rhizoids for anchorage and photosynthetic stems.
 
• Dichotomous Branching: Their stems exhibit dichotomous branching, meaning they split into two equal branches.
 
• Synangia: They reproduce via sporangia fused together into structures called synangia, which produce spores.
 
• Whisk-like Appearance: Their common name "whisk fern" comes from their slender, upright stems.
 
• Related to Ferns: Though simpler in structure, they are classified with ferns in the broader group of Pteridophytes.
 
 
 
• **Dryopteris (Shield Ferns):**
 
 
• True Fern: Dryopteris is a genus of true ferns, belonging to the family Dryopteridaceae.
 
• Vascular Plants: They are vascular plants, meaning they have specialized tissues for transporting water and nutrients.
 
• Fronds: They possess characteristic large, divided leaves called fronds, which are often the most recognizable part of the fern.
 
• Sori: Spores are produced in structures called sori, located on the underside of the fronds.
 
• Habitat: They thrive in moist, shaded environments.
 
• Medicinal Uses: Some species have been used traditionally in herbal medicine.
 
 
 
• **Adiantum (Maidenhair Ferns):**
 
 
• Delicate Fronds: Adiantum ferns are known for their delicate, often lacy fronds, which are often divided into small pinnules.
 
• Distinctive Shape: The shape of the fronds is often described as fan-shaped or maidenhair-like.
 
• Sori Location: Sori are typically located along the margins of the pinnules, often covered by a reflexed flap of tissue.
 
• Habitat: They prefer moist, shady habitats, often growing on rocks or near waterfalls.
 
• Cultivation: Many Adiantum species are popular in horticulture due to their attractive foliage.
 
• Common Name: Known as maidenhair ferns.
